I just wanted to be transparent and let her know that I wanted to take things slow, and she understood that. We made plans on Wednesday night to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie. But here's the thing: I've had an incredibly long week. I only got about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. By the time he asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself, I felt horrible. I was absolutely shattered and knew I would probably just fall asleep. Now, I'm worried that after him thinking I wanted out of the relationship and now canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Ask a Guy, or in this case, an AI) for rescheduling a date when he already has doubts about me? First, I need to consider why I'm canceling the date. It's because I'm extremely tired and not in a good state to enjoy the date. Is it fair to him to go on a date when I'm not fully present? Probably not. It's important to be mentally and emotionally available during dates, especially early on in a relationship. But on the other hand, I don't want him to think that I'm losing interest or that I'm not committed. I need to communicate my reasons clearly and reassure him that I still want to see him, just not tonight. I also need to think about how he might perceive this. If he's already had doubts about me, canceling the date could reinforce those doubts. I should consider whether there's a better way to handle this situation to maintain his trust and interest. Maybe I should have communicated my tiredness earlier or suggested rescheduling sooner. But I didn't, and now I'm in this position. I need to make sure that when I reach out to him, I explain my situation honestly and express my desire to make it up to him on Sunday. It's also important to acknowledge that relationships require communication and understanding. Both partners need to be considerate of each other's needs and circumstances. In this case, I'm prioritizing my well-being, which is important, but I also need to ensure that I'm not neglecting his feelings in the process. Perhaps I should also think about how I can make the next date extra special to show him that I'm still interested and committed. Planning a nice lunch and a movie sounds good, but maybe adding a little something extra could help reassure him. In summary, while it's understandable that I'm canceling the date due to being tired, I need to communicate this clearly and reassure him of my interest. It's a balance between taking care of myself and maintaining his trust and interest in the relationship.
